adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic inverted: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && so a user must be both team admin and owner; should be ||, locking team admins out of the addGuests action (addGuests.handler.ts:44-46)

Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so attendee-triggered mutations update the wrong or no calendar (addGuests.handler.ts:158-163)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code builds the `EventManager` using the acting session user (`const { user } = ctx;` then `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` at ~158-163). But the booking organizer is fetched separately (`organizer` from `booking.userId`) and the calendar event is constructed with organizer metadata. Since the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` path), an attendee-triggered call will attempt `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using the attendee’s credentials instead of the organizer’s, which can update the wrong calendar or fail to update the organizer’s calendar at all. This is a concrete correctness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures are silently swallowed with console.log and the mutation returns success, masking notification failures from users and alerting (addGuests.handler.ts:165-169)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not rethrow or otherwise signal failure (lines ~165-169 in the new file). The handler then proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" }`, so the mutation can succeed even when email notifications fail, masking notification/alerting failures from callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, causing re-sent booking-confirmation emails with ICS REQUEST to already-attending or blacklisted emails (addGuests.handler.ts:166, email-manager.ts:534-540)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (raw input) instead of `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the passed `newGuests` array to decide which template to send per attendee (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) send AttendeeScheduledEmail else AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). If the user re-enters an email that is already an attendee, that email remains in `guests` but is excluded from `uniqueGuests`, so the existing attendee will be treated as a “new guest” and get the booking confirmation email again. The “blacklisted emails get emailed” part is not directly supported by the diff because blacklisted addresses are not added to `calendarEvent.attendees`, and the loop only emails `calendarEvent.attendees`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests are persisted before calendar sync with no transaction; if calendar update fails, retry throws a false 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error since guests are already in the DB (addGuests.handler.ts:82-95, 158-163)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch/compensation. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails but the DB already contains the newly-added guests. On a retry with the same emails, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, which can result in `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and then the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`—misleading because the emails may be valid but already persisted from the failed attempt. This inconsistent state and misleading retry error are directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation error state isInvalidEmail is never cleared on success or dialog close, leaving a stale error banner when the dialog is reopened (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:66-76, 92-102)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails (`handleAdd`), but it is not reset in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (which only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and resets `multiEmailValue`). Also, the dialog’s `onOpenChange` is wired directly to `setIsOpenDialog` with no cleanup, so closing via backdrop/escape can leave `isInvalidEmail` true. As a result, reopening the dialog can show the stale error banner even after a successful add or non-cancel close.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 sentinel throws a raw Prisma P2025 as an unstructured 500 for bookings without an organizer, instead of an explicit tRPC error (addGuests.handler.ts:52-61)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The `|| 0` indicates `booking.userId` may be null/undefined, and in that case the query will look for user id 0 (likely nonexistent) and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "record not found" error (P2025). This exception is not converted into a `TRPCError`, so it would bubble up as an internal/unstructured 500 rather than a controlled tRPC error for bookings lacking an organizer/userId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing-attendee dedup comparison (guest === attendee.email) is case-sensitive, allowing case-variant duplicate attendees for emails already on the booking

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, uniqueGuests is computed by filtering out existing attendees via `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. This comparison is case-sensitive and `guest` is not normalized (nor is attendee.email), so if an existing attendee is `Test@Example.com` and the user adds `test@example.com`, it will not be detected as a duplicate and will be added. The blacklist logic lowercases only the blacklist entries, not `guest`, further indicating a lack of consistent normalization. Thus, the diff introduces/contains a real correctness issue allowing case-variant duplicate attendee emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side uniqueness enforcement within the submitted guest list — duplicate emails in one request pass validation and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows and sends duplicate invitation emails; uniqueness only enforced client-side in AddGuestsDialog.tsx

adjudication.rationale: The server-side `addGuestsHandler` does not de-duplicate emails within the `guests` input array. It computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted ones, but it never removes duplicates present in the submitted `guests` list itself (no `Set`/distinct step). Those duplicates would be passed into `createMany` as repeated rows (`guestsFullDetails` is built directly from `uniqueGuests`), potentially creating duplicate attendee records if the DB schema allows it (or causing an insertion error if a unique constraint exists). Additionally, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses the original `guests` array (not de-duped), so downstream logic can also result in duplicate notifications. Client-side uniqueness is enforced only in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` via a local Zod refine, which can be bypassed by calling the API directly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee-added emails attach the full attendee list to ICS and emails (including replyTo) for seated events with seatsShowAttendees: false, leaking attendee emails the organizer configured to be hidden (addGuests.handler.ts lines ~120-145, email-manager.ts sendAddGuestsEmails)

Unbounded guest list — no max() on the guests array and no handler cap, allowing any authorized attendee to submit thousands of emails creating a spam/email-flooding amplification vector (addGuests.schema.ts)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds addGuests.schema.ts with `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` and the server handler `addGuestsHandler` processes the entire array without any `.max()` constraint or other cap. The UI (`MultiEmail`) also allows adding unlimited entries. The handler then creates attendees via `createMany` and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends emails per attendee, so a permitted caller (including an existing attendee per the `isAttendee` check) could submit a very large list to trigger heavy DB work and an email-flood/amplification scenario. This is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow with id: booking.userId || 0 throws an unhandled 500 when booking.userId is null (possible for team-event bookings) instead of returning a meaningful error (addGuests.handler.ts lines ~62-72)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined`, this becomes `id: 0`, which will not match a real user and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma error. There is no surrounding try/catch converting that into a `TRPCError`, so it will surface as an internal 500 rather than a meaningful domain error. The use of `|| 0` itself indicates the code anticipates `booking.userId` can be falsy, making this a verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guests array (z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max()) allows mass attendee creation, email bombing, and API DoS via unbounded createMany, email fan-out, and calendar updates

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `addGuests` mutation whose input schema is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound (`.max(...)`). The handler then uses `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails })`, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with per-attendee fan-out (organizer + team members + all attendees). With no server-side cap, an authorized caller can submit an extremely large guests array, causing large DB writes, expensive calendar updates, and large email fan-out (potential DoS/spam). This is directly verifiable in the added schema/handler and is not mitigated elsewhere in the diff (only blacklist and dedup vs existing attendees).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Entire email fan-out and calendar update are awaited synchronously before the mutation responds, scaling request duration with attendee count and risking timeouts; retry re-creates attendees and re-sends emails due to dedup running against stale booking.attendees
Overly broad cache invalidation via utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() refetches all bookings queries on every add-guests action instead of invalidating only the affected query

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the mutation `onSuccess` calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()`, which invalidates the entire `viewer.bookings` router cache rather than a specific query (e.g., the booking/detail query for `bookingId`). This is verifiable in the diff and will trigger refetches for all bookings-related queries, making the invalidation broader than necessary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: O(newGuests × attendees) linear scans in addGuests.handler.ts and email-manager.ts hot paths, which compound with the missing input bound; a Set lookup would fix it

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces repeated linear membership checks that make runtime O(guests×attendees): in addGuests.handler.ts each `guest` runs `booking.attendees.some(...)` (linear in existing attendees) and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(...)` (linear in blacklist). In email-manager.ts `sendAddGuestsEmails` maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` and does `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (linear in newGuests) for each attendee, again O(attendees×newGuests). Additionally, the new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` has no upper bound on `guests` length, so an attacker could submit very large arrays and amplify these costs (potential DoS). Using Sets and a max length would address this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog is mounted per booking row with per-render Zod schema construction and hook calls, causing per-render waste in list components; schema should be module-scope and dialog rendered conditionally

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that each `BookingListItem` always renders an `<AddGuestsDialog .../>` instance (even when closed), and `AddGuestsDialog` creates `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` inside the component so it is reconstructed on every render. However, this is a performance/micro-optimization concern rather than a clear bug/correctness/security defect. It’s also consistent with existing patterns in the same file where other dialogs are mounted unconditionally. The claim that this is a “real problem” is therefore not strictly verifiable as a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirst booking lookup at addGuests.handler.ts:33 is not scoped to the caller, allowing any authed user to trigger a full multi-relation fetch for arbitrary booking IDs before authorization check

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `addGuestsHandler` performs `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: { attendees, eventType, destinationCalendar, references, user: { ... }}})` before any authorization check. Because the TRPC procedure is only `authedProcedure`, any logged-in user can supply arbitrary `bookingId` values and force this multi-relation fetch for bookings they don’t have access to, and they can also distinguish `NOT_FOUND` vs `FORBIDDEN` (booking existence leakage) based on the post-fetch checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner condition at addGuests.handler.ts:47-48 appears to be an authorization logic bug excluding admins

adjudication.rationale:
In addGuests.handler.ts the flag is computed as:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

Despite the variable name “isTeamAdminOrOwner”, the logic requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner. If a user is a team admin but not an owner (a common role setup), `isTeamAdminOrOwner` becomes false and they are denied unless they also happen to be the organizer/attendee. This is an authorization logic bug introduced in the diff; it should almost certainly be `||` to match the intended meaning.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses && instead of ||, requiring users to be both team admin AND team owner, locking out team admins with FORBIDDEN error

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning it is only true if the user is BOTH a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will therefore reject users who are team admins but not owners (and not organizer/attendee). Given the variable name and typical authorization intent (admin OR owner), this is a verifiable logic defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest email blacklist comparison is case-sensitive and doesn't trim input, allowing blacklisted emails like 'Foo@Spam.com' or padded emails to bypass the block

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guests` values are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `z.string().email()` accepts uppercase characters, a value like `Foo@Spam.com` will not match a lowercased blacklist entry and will bypass the block. The “doesn't trim input” part is less clearly verifiable because the Zod `.email()` validator likely rejects leading/trailing whitespace anyway, but the case-sensitive bypass is definitely present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server input schema omits uniqueness constraint enforced client-side, allowing direct API callers to send duplicate emails creating duplicate Attendee rows and duplicate emails; attendee-match filter is also case-sensitive creating duplicates

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The client dialog validates uniqueness via `z.array(...).refine(...)`, but the server TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with a `.filter(...)` that only checks against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist, and it does not de-duplicate duplicates within the submitted `guests` array itself. So a direct API caller can pass `guests: ["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` and both entries will pass the filter and be inserted via `createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows/emails (unless a DB unique constraint exists, not shown in the diff). Additionally, the comparisons are case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` while the blacklist is lowercased), allowing duplicates/blacklist bypass via different casing (e.g., `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler passes raw guests array instead of uniqueGuests to sendAddGuestsEmails, causing previously-existing attendees to receive a full scheduled/confirmed email instead of the 'guests added' notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` (and blacklisted), and only those are persisted via `createMany`. However it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input `guests` array, not `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide which template to send: it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` when the email is in `newGuests`, otherwise `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Therefore, if the client includes an email that is already an attendee, that existing attendee will be treated as a “new guest” and receive the full scheduled/confirmed email instead of the 'guests added' notification. This mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status validation — guests can be added to cancelled/pending bookings, persisting attendees and sending confirmed ICS attachments for cancelled events

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches a booking by `id` and then unconditionally updates `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(...)` and sends calendar/email notifications, without checking any booking status (e.g., cancelled, rejected, pending). In the new email templates (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts` / `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), the generated ICS payload hardcodes `status: "CONFIRMED"`, so even if the underlying booking is cancelled, the code would still persist new attendees and send “confirmed” invites/updates. This is directly observable in the diff: there is no status field read or validation before mutation and notifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-transactional write sequence: DB mutation persists then calendar update can fail, returning an error despite persistence; retry then throws misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST error and calendar can never be repaired

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards it calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no transaction and no error handling around the calendar update. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the TRPC mutation fails even though the attendee rows were already persisted. On a retry with the same `guests`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees`, so it becomes empty and the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, preventing a straightforward retry to repair the calendar state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mutation returns hardcoded English string 'Guests added' instead of an i18n key, inconsistent with the error contract that uses translatable keys

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation ends with `return { message: "Guests added" };`, which is indeed a hardcoded English string. However, nothing in the diff shows a contract that success responses must return i18n keys. The client (`AddGuestsDialog`) does not use the returned `message` at all; it displays a toast via `t("guests_added")` on success and uses `t(err.message)` for errors. So while the string is non-i18n, the diff does not demonstrate it causes a correctness/behavior issue or violates an explicit API contract—it's more of a consistency/style preference than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so team admins/owners who aren't the organizer or attendee always get FORBIDDEN error in addGuests.handler.ts

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Despite the variable name implying an OR check, this requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) { throw FORBIDDEN }` will therefore reject a user who is only an admin (or only an owner) and not the organizer/attendee. This is a concrete logic bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist check bypassed via case sensitivity: blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest email is not, so Spam@Example.com bypasses spam@example.com

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is split and lowercased (email.toLowerCase()), but incoming `guest` values from `input.guests` are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates format (`z.string().email()`) and does not lowercase, a mixed-case email like `Spam@Example.com` would not match a lowercased blacklist entry `spam@example.com`, bypassing the blacklist check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-attendee check (guest === attendee.email) is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails for same address with different casing

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees using a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since the input schema `z.string().email()` does not normalize casing, the same email address with different casing (e.g., `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`) will not be detected as a duplicate and can be inserted as an additional attendee row. The dialog-side uniqueness check also uses `new Set(emails)` without lowercasing, so it won’t prevent case-variant duplicates either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side deduplication of guests array within a single request; schema accepts duplicate emails and handler only filters against existing attendees, causing duplicate DB rows and emails
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue points out that the guests array is not deduplicated within a single request and that only existing attendees are filtered out, allowing duplicate emails to result in duplicate DB rows—this is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No compensation/rollback when calendar update fails after DB write: guests are persisted but emails not sent and client sees error, with no retry or cleanup

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterwards `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will fail and return an error to the client, but the attendee rows have already been persisted—there is no transaction/rollback or cleanup in this diff. Additionally, email sending is wrapped in a try/catch that only logs, so failures there result in persisted guests with no emails and no retry mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure is silently swallowed with console.log that omits the error object, no structured logging or monitoring, and mutation returns success

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` call is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and discards the caught `err` (no error details/stack). The handler then continues and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless of whether email sending failed. This is directly verifiable in the diff and means email failures are effectively swallowed with minimal logging while the mutation reports success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No max cap on guests array in schema, allowing unbounded email/calendar fan-out abuse since any attendee can invoke the mutation

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in `addGuests.schema.ts` with no `.max(...)` or other cap. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization allows any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call the mutation, and the handler will (a) `createMany` new attendee records for all `uniqueGuests`, (b) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (c) call `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out over `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` (sending emails per attendee) plus organizer/team members. With no bound on `guests`, an attendee can submit a very large list and trigger unbounded DB writes and email/calendar update fan-out, which is an abuse/security/resource issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager built with ctx.user (caller) credentials instead of booking.user, so attendee-initiated calendar updates run with wrong credentials and may fail or no-op

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation explicitly allows an attendee to call it (isAttendee check). However the calendar update is executed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller), not the booking’s organizer (`booking.user` / `booking.userId`). Since the calendar event being updated corresponds to the booking/organizer’s calendar, running `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with attendee credentials is verifiably inconsistent with the booking ownership and can cause the update to fail/no-op for attendee-initiated calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client error toast fallback t("unable_to_add_guests") is unreachable because message template string is always non-empty, and untranslated server error messages may render as raw keys

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the onError handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. Because `message` is always a (non-empty) string due to template string interpolation (even when `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes e.g. `"undefined: ..."`), the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback will never be used. This is directly verifiable from the diff. Also, since it always renders `t(err.message)` into that string, if `err.message` is a key without a translation it will surface as a raw key-like string instead of using the intended fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail validation state is not reset on successful submission in onSuccess, so stale error warning shows when dialog is reopened

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation in `handleAdd`, but it is never reset in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (which only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`). Because the dialog component stays mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem` and only controlled via `open`), `isInvalidEmail` will remain `true` after a successful submission and the warning can reappear when the dialog is reopened (cancel button resets it, but success does not).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`, which is contradictory (a user can't be both) making it effectively dead code; the intent was `||`

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This requires the user to satisfy *both* predicates, yet the variable name (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`) and the typical access rule implied by the later check (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`) suggest that being either an admin or an owner should grant access. Even if it’s technically possible for one user to be both, using `&&` will incorrectly deny access to users who are only admin or only owner, which is a real correctness/authorization bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx re-declares an inline Zod schema that duplicates and diverges from the shared ZAddGuestsInputSchema (client enforces uniqueness, server does not)

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the client defines an inline schema `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` that rejects duplicate emails. On the server, the shared `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `{ bookingId: number, guests: email[] }` and does not enforce uniqueness. The handler then builds `uniqueGuests` via `guests.filter(...)`, which filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the submitted `guests` array, so duplicates can pass server validation and be written via `createMany`. This is a real divergence between client and server validation and can lead to inconsistent behavior (e.g., duplicates accepted by API despite client preventing them).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side guest filtering in addGuests.handler.ts does not deduplicate within the guests array and uses case-sensitive comparison against existing attendees, letting duplicates through and bypassing the lowercased blacklist

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed via `guests.filter(...)` but it only filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and those in `blacklistedGuestEmails`. It does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array itself (so `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` both pass if not already attendees/blacklisted). Also, both checks are case-sensitive: existing attendees are checked with `guest === attendee.email` and the blacklist is built as lowercased emails but compared with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, allowing case-variant bypasses (e.g., `Bad@x.com`). The server schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` also does not enforce uniqueness, unlike the client-side refine.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarEvent assembly (~50 lines) is duplicated across addGuests.handler, editLocation.handler, and confirm.handler; should be extracted into a shared getCalEventFromBooking helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new CalendarEvent construction block in `addGuests.handler.ts`, but it does not show the implementations of `editLocation.handler` or `confirm.handler`. Without those files in the diff, the claim that the same ~50-line CalendarEvent assembly is duplicated across all three handlers is not verifiable from the provided changes; it may be true in the codebase, but it is speculative based on this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure in addGuests.handler.ts is silently swallowed: error object discarded, console.log used instead of structured logger, and user sees a success toast with no diagnostics

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The catch block discards `err` and does not rethrow, so the mutation still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the client `onSuccess` toast (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`) will show even if email delivery failed. This is a verifiable behavior introduced by the diff and provides no actionable diagnostics beyond a generic `console.log`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx success path does not reset isInvalidEmail, causing a stale validation banner to show when the dialog is reopened

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure in `handleAdd()`, and it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. In the mutation `onSuccess`, the code closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Since the dialog component remains mounted (rendered in `BookingListItem` regardless of open state), reopening the dialog after a prior validation error will still have `isInvalidEmail === true`, causing the validation banner to show immediately even though the inputs were reset.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx uses index-based React keys on a mutable email list, which can misattach in-flight input state (focus, IME composition, validation state) after removals

adjudication.rationale: In packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx, the component renders a mutable list of EmailField inputs via `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}> ...)`. The list is mutated with `splice(index, 1)` on removal and `push("")` on add. Using the array index as the React key in a list where items can be removed/reordered can cause React to reuse DOM nodes for different emails after a deletion, which can misassociate per-input state (focus, ongoing IME composition, internal validation UI/state) with the wrong row. This issue is directly present in the diff and is a known correctness/UX pitfall.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts returns a hardcoded English string 'Guests added' instead of an i18n message key like other handlers in the router

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `addGuests.handler.ts` returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, which is a hardcoded English string. However, nothing in the shown diff indicates this `message` is consumed for user-facing UI or that other booking handlers return i18n keys instead (the proposed comparison to “other handlers” isn’t verifiable here). In the UI added in this diff, success feedback uses `showToast(t("guests_added"), ...)` and does not use the mutation’s returned `message`. So while the string is hardcoded, it’s not a clear correctness/functional defect introduced by the diff based on what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial-failure deadlock in addGuests.handler.ts: prisma.booking.update commits attendees before unguarded updateCalendarAttendees call, so a calendar failure leaves attendees persisted in DB while retry is permanently blocked by the dedup filter throwing misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error; should be wrapped in a transaction or made idempotent

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code persists new attendees via prisma.booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... } }) before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). That calendar update call is not wrapped in try/catch and is not part of a transaction with the DB write, so if updateCalendarAttendees throws, the mutation fails but the new attendees remain committed in the DB. On retry with the same guest emails, uniqueGuests filters out emails already in booking.attendees and then throws BAD_REQUEST when uniqueGuests.length === 0 with message "emails_must_be_unique_valid", which both blocks re-running the calendar update for those guests and is a misleading error for a retry scenario. This partial-failure/inconsistency is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent email delivery failure in addGuests.handler.ts (~line 168): sendAddGuestsEmails errors are swallowed with console.log (error object not logged) and handler returns success 'Guests added', so UI shows success toast with no partial-success flag for the caller

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is wrapped in try/catch that only does console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") and does not log/propagate the caught error. Regardless of email delivery failure, the handler continues and returns { message: "Guests added" }, which will be treated as a successful TRPC mutation. In the UI (AddGuestsDialog), onSuccess shows a success toast (t("guests_added")), so the user will see success even if the email step failed, with no signal of partial failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic bug in addGuests.handler.ts (~line 60): isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring user to be both team admin and team owner, effectively excluding team admins who get FORBIDDEN despite the variable name intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `isTeamAdminOrOwner` in `addGuests.handler.ts` as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to satisfy both checks to be treated as authorized via team role. Given the variable name and the subsequent permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) FORBIDDEN`), this effectively blocks team admins who are not also owners from adding guests, which is a concrete authorization/correctness bug unless the intent was explicitly “owner only”. The `&&` is inconsistent with the name “AdminOrOwner” and common role semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive dedup comparison in addGuests.handler.ts (~lines 70-80): exact-match guest === attendee.email without case normalization creates duplicate attendees and duplicate emails when the same email is entered with different casing

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In addGuests.handler.ts, deduplication against existing attendees is done with a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`), entering the same email with different casing ("User@x.com" vs "user@x.com") will not be treated as a duplicate and will be included in `uniqueGuests`, leading to creating a duplicate attendee record and triggering duplicate/out-of-sync emails/calendar updates. The same case-sensitivity also exists in the client-side uniqueness refine, reinforcing the behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist bypass in addGuests.handler.ts (~lines 70-80): blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but guest is not lowercased before the includes() check, allowing 'Foo@Spam.com' to bypass blacklist entry 'foo@spam.com'

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS are normalized with `.toLowerCase()`, but the incoming `guests` strings are used as-is in the filter: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased (nor otherwise normalized), a case-variant like `Foo@Spam.com` would not match a blacklist entry `foo@spam.com`, allowing bypass. adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status/state check before adding guests: guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, sending ICS REQUEST with status CONFIRMED that resurrects cancelled meetings in attendees' calendars; dialog action also rendered unconditionally in BookingListItem.tsx for cancelled bookings

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation/handler never checks the booking’s state/status before mutating attendees and triggering calendar/email side effects. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, it fetches the booking by `id`, then unconditionally `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and sends emails with ICS data using `status: "CONFIRMED"` in both new email templates. There is no guard like “only allow for ACCEPTED/CONFIRMED bookings” or “block CANCELLED/REJECTED”. Also, in `BookingListItem.tsx` the new action item `{ id: "add_members" ... }` is added to `actions` without any conditional on booking status, so the UI does not prevent invoking it for cancelled/rejected items either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses requester's credentials instead of organizer's: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) is used for EventManager even though ctx.user can be an attendee without access to the organizer's calendar, causing failure/no-op; the correct actor is booking.user

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly allows an attendee to call it (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...);` and it passes the auth check if `isAttendee` is true). Later it builds the calendar update actor from the requester: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` is `ctx.user`. If the requester is an attendee (not the organizer), they generally won’t have the organizer’s calendar credentials needed to update the organizer’s event, yet `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is invoked using only the requester’s credentials. This is a concrete mismatch in the diff and can cause calendar updates to fail/no-op when initiated by non-organizers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Abuse vector: any attendee can programmatically call addGuests with an unbounded list of arbitrary emails (no rate limit, no cap on guests array in ZAddGuestsInputSchema), triggering ICS invites sent from the organizer's address with replyTo: organizer to arbitrary victims — an invitation-spam/phishing channel

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` TRPC mutation is available to any authenticated user who is an attendee of the booking (`isAttendee` check in `addGuests.handler.ts`), not just the organizer/admin. The input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `guests` is an array of emails, with no upper bound on array length and no rate limiting shown. The handler then persists the new attendees and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which sends emails to all attendees including the newly added arbitrary addresses; the email templates generate ICS invites and set `replyTo` to the organizer/attendees (e.g., `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` uses `replyTo: this.calEvent.organizer.email`). This makes it a plausible invitation-spam/phishing vector where an attendee can programmatically add many victim emails and trigger outbound invites/notifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent guest dropping via blacklist: blacklisted emails are filtered out of uniqueGuests with no signal to the caller; partial drops return 'Guests added' misleading the user, and total drops return the wrong error 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by removing emails that are already attendees and any in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(... && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))`). If some inputs are blacklisted but others are not, it proceeds to create only `uniqueGuests` and returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" }`) with no indication that some requested guests were dropped. If all inputs are filtered out, it throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `"emails_must_be_unique_valid"`, which is misleading when the real reason is blacklisting or already-invited guests. This matches the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema doesn't enforce guest uniqueness: uniqueness refine exists only in the client component, so concurrent addGuests mutations (double-click or direct API) both read the same attendees and both createMany, duplicating attendees; should add schema refine and/or unique constraint on (bookingId, email)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. On the server, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` (no uniqueness). In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` filters against existing `booking.attendees` and blacklist, but does not de-duplicate the `guests` array itself, so duplicates in the input (or two concurrent requests that both pass the “not yet an attendee” check) can result in duplicate rows being passed to `attendees.createMany`. There’s also no `skipDuplicates` and no shown DB unique constraint on `(bookingId,email)` in this diff, so duplication is a real correctness risk introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation error state never clears in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (~line 60): isInvalidEmail is only reset on cancel, not on successful handleAdd or input change, so the 'emails must be unique and valid' banner can remain visible during a fixed, valid submission

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails in `handleAdd`, and it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button handler. It is not reset on input change (`MultiEmail` only calls `setMultiEmailValue`) nor before/after a valid submission path. The mutation `onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but does not clear `isInvalidEmail`, so the banner can persist while the user fixes inputs and can reappear if the dialog is closed/reopened without pressing Cancel (e.g., via overlay/onOpenChange).
